actionMeaning.avoid: Do not take this with this condition or medicine. Show a red warning; never auto-schedule.
actionMeaning.doctor_first: Only with their doctor's OK. Ask the person to confirm before scheduling. An item that is already scheduled stays scheduled, with an amber badge, until they confirm.
actionMeaning.caution: Can be fine, but show the reason.
actionMeaning.check_level: A blood test is the way to know. Suggest asking for one.
actionMeaning.may_need_more: This group often needs more of it. Info only, never a dose push.

whenMeaning.forms: Only applies when the ingredient is in one of these forms ("unknown" = the label does not say).
whenMeaning.aboveDaily: Only applies when the planned daily amount from supplements is above this, counted the way the LIMIT counts it (folate = µg folic acid, not DFE; vitamin E = mg_ul; vitamin A = matching forms only), in the nutrient's own unit. A flag whose `when` isn't met is inactive: it shows nothing and does not hide low states.
whenMeaning.withinDaysBeforeSurgery: Only applies from this many days before the operation date until the day of surgery. Taken from pauseBeforeSurgery: stopDaysBefore for paused items; for items that are usually continued, adviceFromDaysBefore (valerian 28) or 14. What the reminder says comes from that row's `advice` (see pauseAdviceMeaning). If upcoming_surgery is set with no date, treat it as inside the window and ask for the date.
whenMeaning.defaulted: The threshold was set automatically to a multivitamin-level amount (an app design choice, not a health limit; or the pregnancy/breastfeeding need if higher), so an ordinary multivitamin is not gated.

pauseAdviceMeaning.pause: Show "Pause from <date>" (operation date minus stopDaysBefore) with the reason.
pauseAdviceMeaning.ask_pause: Show "Ask your team if you should pause this from <date>" with the reason. Some centres list it; harm is not shown.
pauseAdviceMeaning.continue_ask: Show "Usually continued — ask your team" with the reason. Never say "Pause".
pauseAdviceMeaning.taper_ask: From adviceFromDaysBefore days before, show "Ask your team how to taper it" with the reason. Never a sudden stop; the item stays scheduled.
pauseAdviceMeaning.matching: Each ingredient uses its own row(s), respecting `when`; an ingredient with no matching row uses any_supplement. A product the person calls a multivitamin also matches the multivitamin row. An item shows the strictest advice across its ingredients (pauseAdviceOrder) and the earliest date.

badgeMeaning.info: Good to know. No action needed.

groups.any_supplement: Matches every supplement the person takes (used for "tell your doctor about all supplements" rules).
groups.herbal: Ingredients with "herbal": true in ingredients.json, plus ashwagandha and any "other" ingredient. Never vitamins, minerals, multivitamins, foods or medicines.
groups.multivitamin_iron_c: Any product that contains iron or vitamin C.
groups.multivitamin_minerals: Any product that contains calcium, magnesium, iron or zinc.

conditions.name: Pregnancy
conditions.intakeQuestion: Are you pregnant? If so, how many weeks?

flags.label: vitamin_a
flags.why: Do not take vitamin A (retinol) supplements, cod liver oil or liver products. Too much can harm the baby.
alsoWhy: Too much preformed vitamin A can cause birth defects. Avoid liver and high-dose vitamin A supplements, and use only a pregnancy supplement your midwife or doctor approves.

flags.label: St John's wort
flags.why: It may increase the risk of birth defects.

flags.label: berberine
flags.why: Should not be used in pregnancy. It is linked to harm in newborns.

flags.label: ashwagandha
flags.why: Experts advise avoiding it in pregnancy.
alsoWhy: Experts advise against it in pregnancy because of reports of miscarriage risk.

flags.label: ginkgo
flags.why: May cause early labour or extra bleeding at delivery.

flags.label: turmeric
flags.why: Turmeric supplements may be unsafe in pregnancy.

flags.label: fenugreek
flags.why: Not safe in pregnancy in more than food amounts; linked to birth defects.

flags.label: licorice root
flags.why: Large amounts are linked to early delivery.

flags.label: horse chestnut seed extract
flags.why: Not recommended in pregnancy because safety is not known.

flags.label: boron
flags.why: The safety limit is based on harm to unborn young in animal studies, and there is no known benefit. Food amounts are fine.

flags.label: creatine
flags.why: There are no good human trials on creatine safety in pregnancy.

flags.label: nmn
flags.why: EFSA's safety opinion excludes pregnant women.

flags.label: cod liver oil
flags.why: Cod liver oil contains vitamin A as retinol, which is not safe in pregnancy.

flags.label: iodine
flags.why: US thyroid experts advise a 150 µg iodine supplement a day in pregnancy. Ask your midwife what is right for you. Seaweed products vary a lot in iodine.
alsoWhy: Needs rise to 220 µg a day. Thyroid experts advise a 150 µg supplement, but nothing over 500 µg.

flags.label: herbal remedies
flags.why: Not all natural remedies are safe in pregnancy. Check with your pharmacist, midwife or GP first.

flags.label: vitamin_b6
flags.why: B6 can ease pregnancy sickness, but ask first. Long-term high doses can damage nerves; the safe maximum the app uses is 12 mg a day.
alsoWhy: B6 is used for morning sickness, but the doses used are above the EU safe limit. Ask your doctor or midwife first. Daily needs rise to 1.9 mg.

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: Guidelines suggest a daily vitamin D supplement in pregnancy. Your midwife or doctor will advise the dose.
alsoWhy: Take 10 mcg (400 IU) a day from October to March, or all year if you rarely get sun on your skin or have dark skin. Do not take more than 100 mcg a day.

flags.label: coq10
flags.why: Only one study (from 20 weeks) looked at safety in pregnancy.

flags.label: vitamin_a
flags.why: The label does not say if this vitamin A is retinol or beta-carotene. Retinol is not safe in pregnancy. Check the label or ask your midwife.

flags.label: caffeine (including fitness supplements and energy drinks)
flags.why: Keep caffeine under 200 mg a day. Some fitness supplements contain caffeine.

flags.label: calcium
flags.why: Needs are the same as other adults (1,000 mg); ask your midwife or doctor before high doses.

flags.label: magnesium
flags.why: Needs are 350 to 360 mg a day from food and supplements; the supplement limit still applies.

flags.label: probiotics
flags.why: The safety of the yeast probiotic Saccharomyces boulardii in pregnancy has not been established.

flags.label: iron
flags.why: Iron is checked with blood tests during pregnancy. Take iron if your midwife or doctor advises it.
alsoWhy: Needs rise to 27 mg a day; your midwife or doctor will check your blood and advise on iron.

flags.label: vitamin_b9
flags.why: Take 400 mcg folic acid daily until 12 weeks. A higher dose (5 mg) is prescribed if you have diabetes, take epilepsy or HIV medicines, or have a family history of neural tube defects.
alsoWhy: Needs rise to 600 µg DFE. Keep taking folic acid through the first 2 to 3 months.

flags.label: choline
flags.why: Needs rise in pregnancy and most prenatal vitamins contain little or none.
alsoWhy: Most pregnant women get less than they need, and many pregnancy vitamins contain little or none.

flags.label: vitamin_b1
flags.why: Needs rise to 1.4 mg a day.

flags.label: vitamin_b2
flags.why: Needs rise to 1.4 mg a day.

flags.label: vitamin_b3
flags.why: Needs rise to 18 mg a day. Avoid high-dose niacin, as safety data are limited.

flags.label: vitamin_b5
flags.why: Needs rise to 6 mg a day.

flags.label: vitamin_b7
flags.why: Biotin levels often dip in pregnancy. The health effect is unclear.

flags.label: vitamin_b12
flags.why: Needs rise to 2.6 µg a day. Low B12 in pregnancy may harm the baby.

flags.label: zinc
flags.why: Needs rise to 11 mg a day; stay under 25 mg a day.

flags.label: copper
flags.why: Needs rise to 1 mg a day in pregnancy.

flags.label: selenium
flags.why: Needs rise to 60 µg a day. The safe limit still applies.

flags.label: omega_3
flags.why: EFSA suggests an extra 100–200 mg of DHA a day. Choose fish or algal oil, not cod liver oil.

flags.label: fiber
flags.why: Fibre needs rise to 28 g a day in pregnancy. Ask your doctor before using psyllium.

flags.label: protein
flags.why: The RDA rises to 71 g a day in pregnancy.

flags.label: carbohydrates
flags.why: The RDA rises to 175 g a day, and very low-carb plans are not advised in pregnancy.

habits.title: Aim for 150 minutes of moderate activity a week, including 2 strength sessions
habits.why: Exercise is safe in pregnancy and can lower the risk of gestational diabetes and pre-eclampsia.

habits.title: Avoid alcohol
habits.why: There is no known safe level of alcohol in pregnancy.

habits.title: Try ginger for mild sickness
habits.why: Guidelines suggest ginger for mild to moderate pregnancy sickness if you prefer not to take medicine.

habits.title: Eat no more than 2 portions of oily fish a week
habits.why: Oily fish can contain pollutants, such as mercury, that can harm your baby in large amounts.

conditions.name: Breastfeeding
conditions.intakeQuestion: Are you breastfeeding at the moment?

flags.label: diosmin/hesperidin (MPFF)
flags.why: The product information says to avoid it while breastfeeding, as there is no data on breast milk.

flags.label: berberine
flags.why: Should not be used while breastfeeding; it can harm newborns.

flags.label: ashwagandha
flags.why: Should not be used while breastfeeding.
alsoWhy: France's food safety agency advises against it while breastfeeding.

flags.label: St John's wort
flags.why: Breastfed babies of mothers taking it can have colic, drowsiness and lack of energy.

flags.label: horse chestnut seed extract
flags.why: Not recommended because safety while breastfeeding is not known.

flags.label: coq10
flags.why: There is no reliable safety information for breastfeeding.

flags.label: nmn
flags.why: EFSA's safety opinion excludes breastfeeding women.

flags.label: iodine
flags.why: US thyroid experts advise a 150 mcg iodine supplement a day while breastfeeding.

flags.label: ginkgo
flags.why: Little is known about whether ginkgo is safe while breastfeeding.

flags.label: boron
flags.why: There is no proven benefit. Ask your doctor before taking boron supplements.

flags.label: creatine
flags.why: Safety while breastfeeding has not been well studied.

flags.label: caffeine (including green tea extract)
flags.why: High caffeine intake can make breastfed babies fussy and sleep poorly.

flags.label: vitamin_a
flags.why: Your need rises to 1,300 µg a day. Still avoid high-dose vitamin A supplements (over 3,000 µg).

flags.label: probiotics
flags.why: The safety of the yeast probiotic Saccharomyces boulardii while breastfeeding has not been established.

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: Consider 10 mcg (400 IU) vitamin D a day in autumn and winter.

flags.label: vitamin_b12
flags.why: Breastfed babies of mothers who eat no animal foods may have very low B12 reserves. Make sure you get enough B12.
alsoWhy: Needs rise to 2.8 µg a day. Babies of vegan mothers can become low.

flags.label: choline
flags.why: Needs are higher while breastfeeding (550 mg a day).
alsoWhy: The daily need rises to 550 mg while breastfeeding.

flags.label: vitamin_b1
flags.why: Needs rise to 1.4 mg a day.

flags.label: vitamin_b2
flags.why: Needs rise to 1.6 mg a day.

flags.label: vitamin_b3
flags.why: Needs rise to 17 mg a day. Avoid high-dose niacin.

flags.label: vitamin_b5
flags.why: Needs rise to 7 mg a day.

flags.label: vitamin_b6
flags.why: Needs rise to 2 mg a day. Stay under 12 mg a day in total.

flags.label: vitamin_b7
flags.why: Needs rise to 35 µg a day.

flags.label: vitamin_b9
flags.why: Needs rise to 500 µg DFE a day.

flags.label: zinc
flags.why: Needs rise to 12 mg a day; stay under 25 mg a day.

flags.label: copper
flags.why: Needs rise to 1.3 mg a day while breastfeeding.

flags.label: selenium
flags.why: Needs rise to 70 µg a day. The safe limit still applies.

flags.label: iodine
flags.why: Needs rise to 290 µg a day.

flags.label: omega_3
flags.why: EFSA suggests an extra 100–200 mg of DHA a day while breastfeeding.

flags.label: fiber
flags.why: Fibre needs rise to 29 g a day while breastfeeding.

flags.label: protein
flags.why: The RDA rises to 71 g a day while breastfeeding.

flags.label: carbohydrates
flags.why: The RDA rises to 210 g a day, and very low-carb plans are not advised while breastfeeding.

habits.title: Eat at least 2 portions of fish a week, but no more than 2 portions of oily fish
habits.why: Fish is good for you and your baby.

habits.title: Eat plenty of fibre and drink plenty of fluids
habits.why: Fibre can help with bowel problems and constipation after birth.

conditions.name: Trying to get pregnant
conditions.intakeQuestion: Are you trying to get pregnant, or could you become pregnant in the next few months?

flags.label: vitamin_a
flags.why: Avoid high-dose vitamin A (above 3,000 mcg or 10,000 IU a day) if you could become pregnant; too much can cause birth defects.
alsoWhy: The risk to a baby is highest in the first weeks, often before you know you are pregnant. Avoid liver and high-dose vitamin A supplements.

flags.label: cod liver oil
flags.why: Cod liver oil contains vitamin A as retinol, which is not safe in pregnancy.

flags.label: herbal remedies
flags.why: National advice is not to take herbal remedies if you are trying to get pregnant.

flags.label: ashwagandha
flags.why: Food agencies have raised concerns about effects on pregnancy and sex hormones.

flags.label: nmn
flags.why: It is not considered safe in pregnancy, so check with your doctor before trying.

flags.label: vitamin_a
flags.why: The label does not say if this vitamin A is retinol or beta-carotene. Retinol is not safe in pregnancy. Check the label or ask your midwife.

flags.label: boron
flags.why: High doses harmed fertility in animal studies. Keep to food amounts unless your doctor advises otherwise.

flags.label: vitamin_b9
flags.why: Take 400 mcg folic acid daily, ideally from 3 months before pregnancy. Some people need a higher 5 mg prescription dose.
alsoWhy: Take 400 to 800 µg folic acid a day, starting at least 1 month before pregnancy. It lowers the risk of spine and brain birth defects.

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: Consider 10 mcg (400 IU) vitamin D a day, at least in autumn and winter.

flags.label: iodine
flags.why: Thyroid experts advise starting 150 µg a day before pregnancy.

habits.title: Start folic acid at least a month before trying to conceive
habits.why: US experts advise 400 to 800 mcg folic acid a day for anyone who could become pregnant, starting at least 1 month before conception.

Are my medicines and supplements safe if I become pregnant?

conditions.name: Type 1 diabetes
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have type 1 diabetes and use insulin?

flags.label: chromium
flags.why: It may increase the effect of insulin and raise the risk of low blood sugar.
alsoWhy: Chromium may add to insulin's effect and cause low blood sugar.

flags.label: berberine
flags.why: It can lower blood sugar and may add to the effect of insulin.

flags.label: vitamin_e
flags.why: Medical advice is to check with your doctor before taking vitamin E if you have diabetes.

flags.label: vitamin_b9
flags.why: If you plan a pregnancy, UK guidance advises a higher prescribed dose (5 mg). Ask your doctor.

flags.label: potassium
flags.why: Diabetes can affect how the body handles potassium; ask before potassium pills.

flags.label: fiber
flags.why: Talk to your doctor before starting a psyllium supplement.

flags.label: carbohydrates
flags.why: Carbs need to be matched with insulin; set your goal with your diabetes team.

flags.label: ashwagandha
flags.why: It might interact with diabetes medicines.

flags.label: fenugreek
flags.why: Large doses may cause a harmful drop in blood sugar.

flags.label: vitamin_b3
flags.why: High doses can raise blood sugar. Keep to normal amounts.

flags.label: coq10
flags.why: CoQ10 may lower insulin needs, so check your blood sugar.

flags.label: vitamin_b12
flags.why: Type 1 diabetes is listed as a common risk factor for low B12. Ask if a test makes sense for you.
alsoWhy: Autoimmune conditions like type 1 diabetes raise the risk of low B12.

flags.label: vitamin_b1
flags.why: People with diabetes often have lower B1 levels. The health effect is not clear.

habits.title: If you drink alcohol, check your sugar afterwards
habits.why: Alcohol can cause a delayed low when you use insulin.

doctorQuestions: Could any of my supplements change how much insulin I need?
Should I be tested for coeliac disease?
Should my B12 level be checked?

conditions.name: Type 2 diabetes
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told you have type 2 diabetes? Which diabetes medicines do you take, for example metformin, insulin or a tablet that makes your body release more insulin?

flags.label: berberine
flags.why: It can lower blood sugar. With diabetes medicines it may push sugar too low, and it changes how some medicines are handled.

flags.label: chromium
flags.why: It may add to the sugar-lowering effect of diabetes medicines and cause lows. Any benefit is small and unclear.
alsoWhy: Chromium may add to diabetes medicines and cause low blood sugar. Its benefit is unproven.

flags.label: ginseng
flags.why: It might lower blood sugar. Check with your doctor first if you have diabetes.

flags.label: goldenseal
flags.why: In a study it lowered metformin levels by about a quarter, which could weaken sugar control.

flags.label: vitamin_e
flags.why: Medical advice is to check with your doctor before taking vitamin E if you have diabetes.

flags.label: vitamin_b9
flags.why: If you plan a pregnancy, UK guidance advises a higher prescribed dose (5 mg). Ask your doctor.

flags.label: potassium
flags.why: Diabetes can affect how the body handles potassium; ask before potassium pills.

flags.label: carbohydrates
flags.why: There is no single best carb amount; set a personal goal with your care team, especially if you take insulin or SGLT2 inhibitors.

flags.label: ashwagandha
flags.why: It might interact with diabetes medicines.

flags.label: cinnamon
flags.why: Benefit for blood sugar is unclear. Using cinnamon supplements with diabetes medicines can cause unwanted side effects, and large amounts of cassia cinnamon may worsen liver disease.

flags.label: aloe vera (taken by mouth)
flags.why: Using aloe with diabetes medicines can cause unwanted side effects.

flags.label: magnesium
flags.why: Diabetes can lower magnesium, but supplements are not advised just to lower blood sugar. Keep supplements to 250 mg a day or less unless your doctor says otherwise.
alsoWhy: Diabetes can increase magnesium loss; trial doses are above the supplement limit, so ask your doctor first.

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: Trials show little effect on blood sugar in diabetes. Do not go above 4,000 IU (100 mcg) a day unless your doctor advises it.

flags.label: vitamin_b3
flags.why: High-dose niacin can raise blood sugar. The safe maximum from supplements is 10 mg a day as niacin (nicotinic acid), or 35 mg as nicotinamide.
alsoWhy: High doses can raise blood sugar. Keep to normal amounts.

flags.label: fenugreek
flags.why: Large doses may cause a harmful drop in blood sugar.

flags.label: selenium
flags.why: Long-term 200 µg a day was linked to more type 2 diabetes in large trials. Stay near the RDA unless your doctor advises otherwise.

flags.label: fiber
flags.why: Psyllium can lower blood sugar, so check levels if you take diabetes medicines.
alsoWhy: Psyllium fibre taken before meals lowered fasting sugar and HbA1c in trials of people with type 2 diabetes. If you use insulin or sugar-lowering tablets, watch for lows.

flags.label: protein
flags.why: Usual protein advice applies (0.8–1.5 g per kg); if your kidneys are affected, ask your doctor.

flags.label: coq10
flags.why: CoQ10 may lower insulin needs if you use insulin, so check your blood sugar.

flags.label: nmn
flags.why: Trials found no clear effect on blood sugar; don't use it in place of your treatment.

flags.label: vitamin_b12
flags.why: Metformin can lower B12 over time. Ask about a blood test now and then, especially with tingling feet, tiredness or anaemia.
alsoWhy: Metformin can lower B12 over time. Ask for a B12 test.

flags.label: vitamin_b1
flags.why: People with diabetes often have lower B1 levels. High doses for blood sugar are only tested in small trials.

habits.title: Walk for about 10 minutes after each main meal
habits.why: In a trial this lowered sugar after meals more than one daily 30-minute walk, most after the evening meal.

habits.title: Break up long sitting with short, light walks
habits.why: In short lab trials, light walking breaks lowered sugar and insulin after meals compared with sitting still.

habits.title: Do structured exercise: brisk activity, strength work or both
habits.why: Structured exercise lowered HbA1c in many trials; more than 150 minutes a week worked better.

habits.title: Eat more high-fibre foods (at least 14 g fibre per 1,000 calories)
habits.why: Diabetes guidelines advise high-fibre, minimally processed carbohydrate foods.

habits.title: If you drink alcohol, check your sugar afterwards
habits.why: Alcohol can cause a delayed low, especially with insulin or tablets that boost insulin.

conditions.name: Prediabetes (blood sugar higher than normal)
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told your blood sugar is higher than normal but not yet diabetes, sometimes called prediabetes or borderline diabetes?

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: In 3 trials of people with prediabetes pooled together, vitamin D lowered the chance of getting diabetes by about 15%. Ask your doctor if it suits you.
alsoWhy: Trials used about 3,500 to 4,000 IU a day to lower diabetes risk. Agree any dose above the daily amount with your doctor.
US diabetes guidelines do not advise vitamin D for everyone with prediabetes. They note that giving it to millions of people could raise the risk of side effects.

flags.label: berberine
flags.why: It may lower blood sugar, but studies are limited and it can change how other medicines work.

flags.label: chromium
flags.why: Any benefit for blood sugar is small and unclear. Rare cases of liver and kidney problems have been reported.
alsoWhy: Trials found no effect on blood sugar in people without diabetes.

flags.label: cinnamon
flags.why: It is unclear if it helps. Cassia cinnamon contains coumarin, and long-term use may be a problem for people with liver disease.

flags.label: magnesium
flags.why: It may slightly improve how your body uses insulin. Keep supplements to 250 mg a day or less unless your doctor says otherwise.

flags.label: vitamin_b3
flags.why: In a large trial, high-dose niacin led to more new cases of diabetes.

flags.label: selenium
flags.why: Long-term 200 µg a day was linked to more type 2 diabetes in large trials.

flags.label: carbohydrates
flags.why: Ask your doctor about a personal carb goal.

flags.label: nmn
flags.why: One small trial found better insulin sensitivity, but reviews found no clear blood sugar benefit.

flags.label: vitamin_b12
flags.why: If you take metformin long term, ask about B12 checks, especially if you have anaemia or nerve symptoms.
alsoWhy: If you take metformin, it can lower B12 over time. Ask for a B12 test.

flags.label: fiber
flags.why: Psyllium fibre gave a modest drop in blood sugar in people at risk of diabetes.

habits.title: If you are overweight, aim to lose about 7% of your body weight
habits.why: In a large trial, a lifestyle programme cut new diabetes by more than half, and worked better than metformin.

habits.title: Be active for at least 150 minutes a week, like brisk walking
habits.why: This was a core part of the lifestyle programme that prevented diabetes in trials.

habits.title: Take short, light walks during long periods of sitting
habits.why: In short lab trials, light walking breaks lowered sugar and insulin after meals compared with sitting.

How often should my blood sugar (HbA1c) be rechecked?

conditions.name: Kidney disease (reduced kidney function)
conditions.intakeQuestion: Has a doctor told you that your kidneys are not working fully, for example chronic kidney disease, or that you need dialysis or have a kidney transplant?

flags.label: potassium
flags.why: Weak kidneys may not clear potassium, so even normal amounts can build up. Avoid potassium supplements and potassium salt substitutes unless your kidney team agrees.
alsoWhy: Weak kidneys cannot remove potassium, so pills or salt substitutes can cause a dangerous heart rhythm; your kidney team may also limit potassium foods.

flags.label: creatine
flags.why: Kidney experts list creatine as high risk for people with kidney disease.
alsoWhy: Experts advise people with kidney disease to check with their doctor first. Creatine also raises blood creatinine on kidney tests.

flags.label: licorice root
flags.why: Even small amounts have been linked to severe side effects, such as heart rhythm problems, in people with kidney conditions.

flags.label: herbal 'kidney detox' or 'cleanse' products
flags.why: These are not proven and some ingredients can harm the kidneys or interact with medicines.

flags.label: St John's wort
flags.why: Kidney experts list it as high risk because it interacts with many other medicines.

flags.label: magnesium
flags.why: Magnesium can build up to harmful levels when the kidneys are weak.
alsoWhy: Weak kidneys cannot clear extra magnesium, so it can build up to harmful levels.

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: Kidney disease can upset the balance of minerals in bones and blood. Ask your health care team before using vitamin or mineral supplements.
alsoWhy: Your kidneys help activate vitamin D and control calcium. Let your doctor set the dose.

flags.label: protein
flags.why: Some people with kidney disease need moderate protein so waste does not build up, but too little can cause poor nutrition. Ask a dietitian how much is right.
alsoWhy: Kidney disease often needs a lower protein limit (guidelines use about 0.55–0.8 g per kg), set by your kidney team.

flags.label: vitamin_c
flags.why: With kidney problems, extra vitamin C can raise stone-forming substances in urine. Ask your doctor for a safe dose.
alsoWhy: High intakes may raise oxalate in urine and could add to kidney stones, especially in people with kidney problems.

flags.label: vitamin_b3
flags.why: In people on dialysis, high-dose nicotinamide caused low platelets and loose stools.

flags.label: vitamin_b6
flags.why: Kidney disease can lower B6, but a high-dose B vitamin mix sped up kidney decline in a trial of diabetic kidney disease.

flags.label: vitamin_b9
flags.why: A high-dose mix of folic acid, B6 and B12 sped up kidney decline in a trial of diabetic kidney disease.

flags.label: vitamin_b12
flags.why: A high-dose mix of B12, folic acid and B6 sped up kidney decline in a trial of diabetic kidney disease.

flags.label: calcium
flags.why: Your kidneys help control calcium, so your care team should set your calcium amount.

flags.label: iron
flags.why: Kidney disease often needs a different iron plan set by your kidney team.
alsoWhy: In anaemia caused by kidney disease, iron is guided by regular blood tests from your kidney team.

flags.label: selenium
flags.why: People on dialysis can run low on selenium. Your kidney team should guide any dose.

flags.label: chromium
flags.why: People with kidney disease may be more sensitive, and high doses have been linked to kidney damage.
alsoWhy: People with kidney disease may be more sensitive to harm from high chromium intakes.

flags.label: molybdenum
flags.why: Your kidneys clear molybdenum, so ask your doctor before taking it.

flags.label: boron
flags.why: Boron leaves the body through the kidneys.

flags.label: silicon
flags.why: The kidneys clear silicon, and blood levels rise when they don't work well.

flags.label: collagen
flags.why: Collagen adds to your protein total, which may need limiting in kidney disease.

flags.label: fiber
flags.why: Tell your doctor before using psyllium if you have kidney disease.

flags.label: green or 'superfood' powders, seaweed and electrolyte products
flags.why: These can be high in potassium or phosphorus.

flags.label: carbohydrates
flags.why: Very low-carb eating plans are not advised for people with kidney disease.

habits.title: Ask for advice on potassium, phosphate, salt and calories for your stage
habits.why: Guidelines advise diet advice matched to how severe the kidney disease is.

habits.title: Exercise, keep a healthy weight and do not smoke
habits.why: Advised for adults with kidney disease in national guidance.

habits.title: Cut down on processed foods with added phosphate
habits.why: Added phosphate in processed foods raises blood phosphorus more than natural sources.

habits.title: Use herbs and spices instead of salt substitutes
habits.why: Many salt substitutes are high in potassium.

Which of my vitamins or supplements are safe for my kidneys?

conditions.name: Kidney stones
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you ever had kidney stones?

flags.label: calcium
flags.why: Calcium pills, but not calcium from food, have been linked to more kidney stones.
alsoWhy: One large study linked calcium supplements to more kidney stones, but later reviews did not. Keep calcium in your diet and ask your doctor about supplements.

flags.label: collagen
flags.why: Collagen and gelatin can raise oxalate in the urine (5–10 g did so in a study), which matters for stone formers.

flags.label: vitamin_c
flags.why: High doses raise oxalate in urine, which may add to kidney stones.
alsoWhy: High doses (1,000 mg a day or more) are linked to more kidney stones in men. Keep to low doses.

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: Too much vitamin D can raise calcium and cause kidney stones. Stay within 4,000 IU (100 mcg) a day unless your doctor advises more.
alsoWhy: High calcium with vitamin D has been linked to more kidney stones. Keep to the daily amount unless your doctor advises more.

flags.label: turmeric
flags.why: Turmeric supplements may raise the risk of kidney stones. Ask first if stones run in your family.

flags.label: silicon
flags.why: Long-term high silicon from some antacids has been linked to rare silica stones.

habits.title: Drink 2.5 to 3 litres of water a day, unless your doctor has told you to limit fluids
habits.why: Pale urine is a sign you are drinking enough.

habits.title: Keep salt under 6 g a day, get enough calcium in your diet, and limit fizzy, caffeinated and alcoholic drinks
habits.why: Advised to help prevent kidney stones.

doctorQuestions: What type of stone did I have, and does it change what I should eat or drink?
Are my calcium, vitamin C and vitamin D supplements safe for me?
How much fluid should I drink each day?

conditions.name: Liver disease
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told you have a liver condition, such as fatty liver, hepatitis or cirrhosis?

flags.label: kava
flags.why: Kava has been linked to rare but serious liver injury.

flags.label: manganese
flags.why: A damaged liver clears manganese poorly, and it can build up in the brain. Avoid manganese supplements unless your doctor advises them.
alsoWhy: People with long-term liver disease clear manganese poorly and are more likely to be harmed by high intakes.

flags.label: ashwagandha
flags.why: It has caused liver injury, and deaths have been reported in people with advanced liver disease.
alsoWhy: A few reports link ashwagandha to liver problems.

flags.label: turmeric
flags.why: Liver damage has been reported in some people taking high-absorption curcumin products.

flags.label: green tea extract
flags.why: Liver injury has been reported, mostly with green tea extract tablets or capsules.

flags.label: black cohosh
flags.why: Rare cases of liver damage, some very serious, have been reported with products labelled as black cohosh.

flags.label: vitamin_a
flags.why: Liver disease makes vitamin A harm more likely. Only take vitamin A supplements if your doctor advises it.

flags.label: vitamin_e
flags.why: Medical advice is to check with your doctor before taking vitamin E if you have liver disease.

flags.label: choline
flags.why: Choline matters for the liver, but very high doses can harm it. Ask your doctor for the right amount.

flags.label: vitamin_b3
flags.why: High-dose niacin can harm the liver. Keep to normal amounts unless your doctor says otherwise.

flags.label: copper
flags.why: Some liver diseases, especially ones that slow bile flow, can make copper build up in the liver.

flags.label: chromium
flags.why: People with liver disease may be more sensitive to high chromium intakes.

flags.label: cinnamon
flags.why: Long-term use of cassia cinnamon, which contains coumarin, could be a problem for people with liver disease.

flags.label: vitamin_b3
flags.why: High doses of niacin taken for months or years can damage the liver.

flags.label: coq10
flags.why: Long-term use of 300 mg a day has raised liver enzymes in some people.

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: Some liver diseases reduce fat absorption, which can lower vitamin D. Ask about a blood test.

habits.title: Stop a supplement and see a doctor if you get dark urine, yellow skin or eyes, tiredness, nausea or poor appetite
habits.why: These can be signs of liver damage.

doctorQuestions: Which supplements are safe for my liver?
How much alcohol, if any, is safe for me?
Should my liver blood tests be checked before I start a new supplement?

conditions.name: Heart disease
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have a heart condition, such as angina, a past heart attack, heart failure or an irregular heartbeat?

flags.label: licorice root
flags.why: Licorice can cause irregular heartbeat and even cardiac arrest. Even small amounts are linked to severe effects in people with heart conditions.

flags.label: St John's wort
flags.why: It can weaken some heart medicines, such as digoxin and ivabradine.

flags.label: ashwagandha
flags.why: France's food safety agency advises people with heart problems not to use it.

flags.label: potassium
flags.why: Some heart and blood pressure medicines raise potassium. Do not take potassium supplements or potassium salt substitutes unless your doctor agrees.
alsoWhy: Many heart medicines change potassium levels, so ask before any potassium pills.

flags.label: vitamin_e
flags.why: Vitamin E did not prevent heart problems in trials, and one trial found more heart failure. Ask your doctor first.

flags.label: vitamin_b3
flags.why: High-dose niacin did not prevent heart attacks or strokes in large trials and caused harm. Only take it if prescribed.

flags.label: omega_3
flags.why: The risk of an irregular heartbeat rises with dose, especially above 1 g a day.

flags.label: coq10
flags.why: Heart failure studies used CoQ10 alongside usual care, not instead of it.

flags.label: omega_3
flags.why: In two large trials, 4 g a day of omega-3 for several years slightly raised the risk of an irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation) in people with or at high risk of heart disease.

flags.label: calcium
flags.why: Some reviews linked calcium supplements to heart disease, but other studies found no link.
alsoWhy: Some trials linked calcium pills to more heart attacks; get calcium from food where you can and ask your doctor.

flags.label: vitamin_e
flags.why: Vitamin E supplements were linked to more bleeding strokes in two trials.

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: If you take digoxin, calcium with vitamin D can make it stronger. Ask your doctor first.

flags.label: choline
flags.why: Choline raises TMAO, a substance some studies link to heart disease, though choline intake itself was not linked. Stay at the daily need.

flags.label: vitamin_b7
flags.why: Biotin can make heart attack blood tests look normal when they are not. Tell staff you take it.

flags.label: vitamin_b9
flags.why: In heart patients, folic acid with B12 did not prevent heart events, and one trial linked it to more cancer.

flags.label: vitamin_b1
flags.why: Furosemide can lower thiamin (vitamin B1), and low thiamin is common in heart failure.
alsoWhy: People with heart failure, especially on water pills, often run low on B1. Ask your doctor.

flags.label: iron
flags.why: People with heart failure are more likely to have low iron; ask your doctor to check.

habits.title: Do aerobic and muscle-strengthening activity at a level that is safe for you
habits.why: Advised for people with or at high risk of heart disease.

habits.title: Swap saturated fats for olive or rapeseed oil
habits.why: Advised for people at high risk of or with heart disease.

doctorQuestions: Which supplements are safe with my heart medicines?
Should my potassium or kidney function be checked?
How much exercise is safe for me, and should I join a rehab programme?

conditions.name: High blood pressure
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told you have high blood pressure? Do you take medicine for it?

flags.label: potassium salt substitutes
flags.why: Not advised for older people, people with diabetes or kidney disease, pregnant women, or people on ACE inhibitors or ARBs.

flags.label: licorice root
flags.why: Even small amounts have been linked to severe side effects in people with high blood pressure.

flags.label: magnesium
flags.why: Blood pressure trials used about 300 to 400 mg a day, above the supplement limit; keep taking your medicine.

flags.label: potassium
flags.why: Many blood pressure medicines raise potassium; eat potassium-rich food unless your doctor has told you to limit it.

flags.label: ashwagandha
flags.why: It might interact with blood pressure medicines.

flags.label: magnesium
flags.why: Calcium, magnesium and potassium supplements are not advised as a way to lower blood pressure.

flags.label: caffeine (coffee, energy drinks, pre-workout products)
flags.why: Too much coffee and other caffeine-rich products is discouraged for people with high blood pressure.

flags.label: green tea extract
flags.why: Side effects of green tea extract supplements include increased blood pressure.

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: Some water pills for blood pressure (thiazides) can raise blood calcium with vitamin D. Ask your doctor before going above the daily amount.

flags.label: calcium
flags.why: If you take a thiazide water pill, ask your doctor before calcium supplements.

flags.label: coq10
flags.why: CoQ10 does not lower blood pressure in a meaningful way, so keep taking your blood pressure medicines.

habits.title: Keep salt low
habits.why: Less salt can lower blood pressure.

habits.title: Eat a healthy diet and exercise regularly
habits.why: Both can lower blood pressure.

habits.title: Cut down on alcohol if you drink a lot
habits.why: This can lower blood pressure and has other health benefits.

doctorQuestions: What should my blood pressure be?
Are my supplements or salt substitute safe with my blood pressure medicines?
Should my kidney function and potassium be checked?

conditions.name: High cholesterol
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told you have high cholesterol? Do you take a statin or another cholesterol medicine?

flags.label: red yeast rice
flags.why: Some products contain a statin-like drug in unknown amounts, with the same possible side effects and interactions as statins.

flags.label: vitamin_b3
flags.why: High-dose niacin improves blood fats but did not prevent heart events, and caused side effects. Don't self-treat.
alsoWhy: Added to statins in large trials, high-dose niacin did not cut heart events, and one trial found more strokes.

flags.label: vitamin_b5
flags.why: Pantethine at 600 to 900 mg a day lowered LDL a little in small trials. Talk to your doctor; it is not a swap for prescribed medicine.

flags.label: plant stanols or sterols
flags.why: Not advised as a way to prevent heart disease.

flags.label: omega_3
flags.why: UK guidance says there is no evidence that omega-3 products help prevent heart disease, except one prescription form.
alsoWhy: 4 g doses are prescription treatments for very high blood fats and can raise LDL ('bad') cholesterol in some people. Use them only with a doctor.

flags.label: coq10
flags.why: If you take a statin, keep taking it; CoQ10 for statin aches has mixed evidence.

flags.label: fiber
flags.why: About 10 g of psyllium a day can lower LDL ('bad') cholesterol.

habits.title: Keep saturated fat low and use olive or rapeseed oil
habits.why: Advised for people at high risk of heart disease.

habits.title: Do aerobic and muscle-strengthening activity
habits.why: Advised for people at high risk of heart disease.

doctorQuestions: What is my overall heart risk, and do I need a statin?
Are my supplements safe with my cholesterol medicine?
When should my cholesterol be rechecked?

conditions.name: Varicose veins or long-term vein problems in the legs
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have varicose veins, or legs that often feel heavy, achy or swollen, with skin changes or sores around the ankles?

flags.label: horse chestnut (raw seeds, bark, flowers or leaves)
flags.why: These parts are unsafe to take by mouth. Only standardised seed extract has been used safely in studies, for up to 12 weeks.

flags.label: horse chestnut seed extract
flags.why: See a doctor first if you have skin inflammation, a hard or painful vein, severe pain, ulcers, sudden swelling of one or both legs, or heart or kidney failure. Not recommended in pregnancy or breastfeeding.
alsoWhy: In short-term trials, horse chestnut seed extract eased leg pain and swelling. Larger trials are still needed.

flags.label: vein medicines in general (venoactive products)
flags.why: As a group, they ease swelling a little but do not clearly improve quality of life, and they slightly increase side effects.

flags.label: diosmin/hesperidin (MPFF)
flags.why: In placebo-controlled trials it eased leg pain, heaviness, cramps and swelling. Common side effects are stomach upsets such as diarrhoea and nausea. Avoid while breastfeeding.

habits.title: Exercise regularly, for example walking
habits.why: A European vein guideline advises exercise to reduce vein symptoms.

habits.title: Do exercises that strengthen your calf muscles
habits.why: In a small trial in people with severe vein disease, 6 months of calf exercise improved calf pump function and strength, though symptom scores did not change.

habits.title: Try compression stockings for aching or swelling, if a professional says they suit you
habits.why: A European vein guideline recommends stockings of at least 15 mmHg at the ankle to ease symptoms.

habits.title: Ask whether vein treatment would suit you better than stockings
habits.why: UK guidance offers stockings mainly when vein treatment is not suitable.

habits.title: Ask a professional to check stockings are safe for you
habits.why: Stockings are usually safe when used correctly and after checking for reasons not to use them. Skin irritation, discomfort and pain are the most common problems; serious harm is very rare.

habits.title: Raise your legs when resting and avoid standing or sitting still for long periods
habits.why: Symptoms are often worse after standing and better with your legs up.

habits.title: Keep to a healthy weight and do not smoke
habits.why: Advised for varicose veins; smoking damages your veins.

habits.title: Know when to get help
habits.why: See a GP for painful, itchy or swollen legs or a sore that has not healed after 2 weeks. Get urgent help if a vein bleeds.

doctorQuestions: Do I need a scan or a referral to a vein specialist?
Are compression stockings safe for me, and which pressure and length should I use?
Is a vein supplement safe with my other medicines?
What signs mean I should get help quickly, such as a painful, red or swollen leg?

conditions.name: Taking a blood thinner
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you take a medicine to thin your blood or prevent clots, such as warfarin, apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, aspirin or clopidogrel?

flags.label: St John's wort
flags.why: It can weaken warfarin and many other important medicines.

flags.label: ginkgo
flags.why: May increase bleeding risk with blood thinners such as warfarin.

flags.label: horse chestnut seed extract
flags.why: Some horse chestnut products may increase bleeding with blood thinners.

flags.label: coq10
flags.why: CoQ10 may interact with warfarin.
alsoWhy: CoQ10 may change how warfarin works.

flags.label: ginseng
flags.why: Ginseng may interfere with blood clotting.

flags.label: vitamin_e
flags.why: Vitamin E can thin the blood. On blood thinners or daily aspirin, only take a supplement if your doctor agrees.

flags.label: omega_3
flags.why: Fish oil may add to the effect of blood thinners such as warfarin.

flags.label: vitamin_k
flags.why: Only warfarin is affected by vitamin K. If you take warfarin, keep vitamin K steady and ask your doctor before any supplement with it.
alsoWhy: Vitamin K changes how warfarin-type blood thinners work. Keep intake steady and never start or stop it without your doctor.

flags.label: vitamin_e
flags.why: Large doses of vitamin E with blood thinners can increase the risk of bleeding.

flags.label: garlic
flags.why: Garlic supplements may increase bleeding.

flags.label: turmeric
flags.why: Turmeric may increase bleeding with blood thinners.

flags.label: omega_3
flags.why: High-dose fish oil can affect platelets. On warfarin, your INR (a blood clotting test) may need checking.

flags.label: vitamin_b3
flags.why: In a large trial, high-dose niacin led to more bleeding. Ask your doctor first.

habits.title: Eat steady amounts of vitamin K foods, like leafy greens, from week to week
habits.why: On warfarin, avoid sudden large changes in these foods.

habits.title: Tell your clinic before you start or stop any supplement
habits.why: Many supplements change bleeding risk or how blood thinners work.

doctorQuestions: Which supplements are safe with my blood thinner?
If I take warfarin, how much vitamin K food is OK and when should my INR (blood clotting test) be checked?
What signs of bleeding should make me get help?

conditions.name: Surgery or a procedure coming up
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have an operation or procedure planned, including dental surgery? Roughly when?

flags.label: garlic
flags.why: Garlic supplements may increase bleeding. Tell your team, especially before surgery.

flags.label: ginkgo
flags.why: Linked to bleeding. Stop before surgery as your team advises.

flags.label: ginseng
flags.why: Linked to bleeding and low blood sugar.

flags.label: St John's wort
flags.why: It speeds up how the body breaks down many medicines used around surgery.

flags.label: kava
flags.why: Kava can increase the effect of anaesthesia.

flags.label: vitamin_e
flags.why: Guidance based on a 2021 expert consensus says to hold vitamin E for 2 weeks because of a theoretical bleeding risk.
alsoWhy: Stop vitamin E supplements 2 weeks before surgery, as they may raise bleeding risk. Tell your surgeon what you take.

flags.label: turmeric
flags.why: Guidance based on a 2021 expert consensus says to hold turmeric for 2 weeks because of a theoretical bleeding risk.

flags.label: ashwagandha
flags.why: Experts do not recommend it for people about to have surgery.

flags.label: all herbal and dietary supplements
flags.why: Tell your team about every supplement. Anaesthetists may ask you to stop supplements at least 2 weeks before.

flags.label: valerian
flags.why: Ask how to taper it in the weeks before surgery. Do not stop suddenly after long use.

flags.label: omega_3
flags.why: Some professionals advise stopping fish oil, but a large heart-surgery trial found it did not increase bleeding. Follow your team's advice.
alsoWhy: A large trial found fish oil did not raise bleeding in heart surgery, but tell your surgical team what you take.

flags.label: vitamin_b7
flags.why: Biotin can upset blood tests done before surgery. Tell your care team you take it.

flags.label: iron
flags.why: If you have iron-deficiency anaemia, guidelines advise iron tablets before and after surgery.

habits.title: Bring all your supplement bottles to your pre-surgery check
habits.why: Many people forget to mention supplements. Seeing the bottles helps the team plan safely.

habits.title: Ask what you can eat and drink before the operation
habits.why: Guidelines allow clear drinks up to 2 hours and food up to 6 hours before anaesthesia. Always follow your own team's instructions.

habits.title: Ask if you are at risk of poor nutrition
habits.why: People who are poorly nourished may be given nutrition drinks before major surgery.

doctorQuestions: Which of my supplements should I stop, and exactly when?
Should I keep taking my usual medicines, such as blood thinners, metformin or weight-loss injections, up to surgery?
Should I have a blood test for anaemia or low iron before surgery?
When can I restart my supplements afterwards?

conditions.name: Recent surgery (recovering)
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you had an operation in the last few weeks? What kind, and are you still healing?

flags.label: garlic, ginkgo, ginseng and high-dose vitamin E
flags.why: These can increase bleeding. Ask before restarting while wounds heal.

flags.label: garlic, ginkgo, ginseng and high-dose vitamin E
flags.why: These can increase bleeding. Ask before restarting while wounds heal.

flags.label: garlic, ginkgo, ginseng and high-dose vitamin E
flags.why: These can increase bleeding. Ask before restarting while wounds heal.

flags.label: garlic, ginkgo, ginseng and high-dose vitamin E
flags.why: These can increase bleeding. Ask before restarting while wounds heal.
alsoWhy: Ask your surgeon when it is safe to restart vitamin E.

flags.label: probiotics
flags.why: Rare but serious infections have happened in very ill hospital patients, especially with a central line or tube feeding.

flags.label: collagen
flags.why: One small trial found collagen helped pressure sores shrink. This evidence is from pressure sores, not surgical wounds.

flags.label: vitamin_b7
flags.why: Biotin can upset blood tests done after surgery, including heart tests. Tell your care team you take it.

flags.label: vitamin_c
flags.why: High-dose vitamin C did not speed up healing of pressure sores in a trial.

flags.label: zinc
flags.why: Low zinc can slow wound healing in older adults. Taking 50 mg or more a day for weeks can lower copper.

flags.label: iron
flags.why: If you have iron-deficiency anaemia, guidelines advise iron after surgery too.

flags.label: protein
flags.why: Not eating enough after major surgery raises the risk of problems. Ask your team how much food and protein you need.
alsoWhy: Recovery after surgery raises protein needs (about 1.5 g per kg in hospital guidance); follow your care team.

habits.title: Eat and drink as soon as your team allows
habits.why: Starting to eat within hours of most operations is advised.

habits.title: Get up and move as early as your team advises
habits.why: Early movement helps the body use protein and keeps muscles working.

habits.title: Learn the signs of a blood clot
habits.why: Pain and swelling in one leg needs an urgent check. Chest pain or breathlessness needs emergency help.

doctorQuestions: Which supplements can I restart, and when?
Should I take extra protein or a nutrition drink while I recover?
Do I need a blood test for iron or anaemia?
What warning signs in my wound or legs should I watch for?

conditions.name: Thyroid condition
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have a thyroid condition, such as an underactive or overactive thyroid, Hashimoto's or Graves' disease? Do you take thyroid tablets such as levothyroxine?

flags.label: ashwagandha
flags.why: Experts do not recommend it for people with thyroid disorders, and it might interact with thyroid hormone medicine.
alsoWhy: It can change thyroid hormone levels, and cases of an overactive thyroid have been reported.

flags.label: iodine
flags.why: People with autoimmune thyroid disease may get side effects even at iodine amounts that are safe for others. Seaweed products vary a lot in iodine.
alsoWhy: People with thyroid conditions can react badly to iodine amounts that are safe for others.

flags.label: St John's wort
flags.why: Listed as not mixing well with levothyroxine.

flags.label: selenium
flags.why: Selenium can lower thyroid antibodies, but the health benefit is unclear. Thyroid experts advise against it for thyroid antibodies in pregnancy.

flags.label: calcium
flags.why: Calcium can block levothyroxine. Take them at least 4 hours apart.
alsoWhy: Calcium can block thyroid medicine; keep them at least 4 hours apart.

flags.label: iron
flags.why: Iron can block levothyroxine. Take them at least 4 hours apart.
alsoWhy: Iron can block thyroid medicine; keep them at least 4 hours apart.

flags.label: vitamin_b7
flags.why: High-dose biotin can make thyroid blood tests look falsely high or low. Tell your doctor before a test.
alsoWhy: Biotin can upset thyroid blood tests and has led to wrong diagnoses. Tell your doctor before any test.

flags.label: selenium
flags.why: Trial results in autoimmune thyroid disease are mixed. Do not go above 255 µg a day in total.

flags.label: chromium
flags.why: A small study found it reduced levothyroxine absorption. Ask a pharmacist how to space them.
alsoWhy: Chromium can reduce absorption of thyroid hormone tablets. Take them hours apart.

flags.label: fiber
flags.why: Foods with soy, walnuts and dietary fibre may affect how levothyroxine works. Keep your routine the same each day.

flags.label: vitamin_b12
flags.why: Autoimmune thyroid disease raises the risk of low B12.

flags.label: vitamin_b2
flags.why: An underactive thyroid can lower B2 levels.

habits.title: Take levothyroxine on an empty stomach, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast, coffee or other medicines
habits.why: Some foods can affect how it works.

habits.title: Keep calcium and iron supplements at least 4 hours away from levothyroxine
habits.why: These minerals can stop the tablet being absorbed.

doctorQuestions: Is my levothyroxine dose right, and when should my thyroid be rechecked?
Should I pause biotin before my next thyroid blood test?
Are iodine, selenium or herbal products safe for my thyroid condition?

conditions.name: Haemochromatosis (iron overload)
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told you have haemochromatosis or too much iron in your body?

flags.label: iron
flags.why: Do not take iron supplements; they may be harmful when iron is already high.
alsoWhy: Your body already stores too much iron; avoid iron and vitamin C supplements.

flags.label: vitamin_c
flags.why: High doses of vitamin C could make iron overload worse.
alsoWhy: Vitamin C boosts iron uptake and may worsen iron overload. Avoid supplements unless your doctor agrees.

flags.label: multivitamins with iron or vitamin C
flags.why: Treatment includes avoiding iron and vitamin C supplements, so check multivitamin labels.

flags.label: iron-fortified breakfast cereals
flags.why: Avoid cereals with added iron.

habits.title: Keep alcohol low
habits.why: Alcohol can increase iron in the body and strain the liver.

habits.title: Do not eat raw oysters or clams
habits.why: They can carry bacteria that cause serious infections in people with high iron.

doctorQuestions: How often do I need venesection (blood removal), and what are my iron targets?
Is my liver healthy?
Which supplements and multivitamins are safe for me?

conditions.name: Low iron or iron-deficiency anaemia
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told your iron is low or that you have iron-deficiency anaemia? Are you taking iron tablets?

flags.label: iron
flags.why: Treat it only after a blood test, with a doctor who sets the dose and looks for the cause.

flags.label: iron
flags.why: In a small trial in women with low iron, one morning dose on alternate days was absorbed better than daily or split doses. Ask your doctor before changing how you take it.
alsoWhy: Take iron tablets as your doctor advises, usually for about 6 months, with repeat blood tests to check progress.

flags.label: calcium
flags.why: Calcium may get in the way of iron absorption. Take calcium and iron supplements at different times.
alsoWhy: Calcium can lower iron absorption; take iron and calcium at different times.

flags.label: zinc
flags.why: High zinc doses over weeks can lower copper. Stay within 25 mg a day in total.
alsoWhy: Iron pills can lower zinc absorption; take them at different times.

flags.label: manganese
flags.why: Low iron increases manganese absorption and can make manganese toxicity worse.
alsoWhy: Low iron makes the body absorb more manganese.

habits.title: Take iron with or soon after food if it upsets your stomach
habits.why: This can reduce side effects such as feeling sick and constipation.

habits.title: Drink a glass of orange juice after your iron tablet
habits.why: This may help your body absorb the iron.

habits.title: Avoid tea, coffee and milk around the time you take iron
habits.why: These can stop your body absorbing iron.

habits.title: Eat iron-rich foods such as meat, beans, lentils, dark green vegetables and fortified cereals
habits.why: Your GP may advise more iron-rich foods if diet is part of the cause.

doctorQuestions: What is causing my low iron, and do I need more tests?
How long should I take iron, and when will you recheck my blood?
Should I take iron every day or every other day?
What should I do if the tablets upset my stomach?

conditions.name: Low vitamin B12
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told your vitamin B12 is low, or do you have B12 injections or tablets?

flags.label: vitamin_b9
flags.why: High folic acid can hide low B12 and let nerve damage worsen. Get B12 treated first.

flags.label: vitamin_b12
flags.why: Treatment needs a doctor. Tablets of 1,000 µg a day or injections are used.

flags.label: vitamin_b9
flags.why: Large amounts of folic acid can correct the anaemia of B12 deficiency but not the nerve damage, so the problem can be missed. Stay within 1,000 mcg a day unless your doctor advises more.

flags.label: vitamin_b12
flags.why: Follow your doctor's plan. Some people need injections for life, others tablets, depending on the cause.

habits.title: Eat B12 foods or fortified foods if your diet is low in animal foods
habits.why: Fortified cereals, yeast extracts and soy products can help.

doctorQuestions: What is causing my low B12?
Do I need injections or tablets, and for how long?
Could any of my medicines, such as metformin or stomach acid tablets, be a cause?

conditions.name: Low vitamin D
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told your vitamin D is low, or are you rarely outdoors in daylight?

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: Do not take more than 100 mcg (4,000 IU) a day unless your doctor advises it. Too much over a long time can raise calcium and damage the kidneys and heart.
alsoWhy: A blood test shows how low you are. Doses to correct a low level are higher than the meter, and your doctor should set them.
Adults need 10 mcg (400 IU) a day. Take it all year if you are rarely outdoors, live in a care home or cover most of your skin; consider it all year if you have dark skin.

flags.label: vitamin_b7
flags.why: Biotin can upset vitamin D blood test results. Tell the lab before testing.

habits.title: Get some daylight on your skin from late March to September
habits.why: Most people make enough vitamin D from summer sun.

doctorQuestions: What dose of vitamin D do I need, and for how long?
Do I need a repeat blood test?
Are any of my medicines affecting my vitamin D?

conditions.name: Osteoporosis or weak bones
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told you have osteoporosis or thin bones, or had a broken bone from a minor fall?

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: Your doctor may already include vitamin D in your bone care. Follow the dose they give.

flags.label: vitamin_k
flags.why: Results for bones are mixed. Ask your doctor before using vitamin K for bones, and do not use it in place of bone medicine.

flags.label: calcium
flags.why: Calcium supplements are absorbed best in doses of 500 mg or less. Bone tablets like alendronic acid must be taken apart from calcium.
alsoWhy: Bone medicines need enough calcium; your doctor will say if you need a supplement and when to take it.

flags.label: vitamin_a
flags.why: More than 1,500 mcg vitamin A a day over many years may make bones more likely to break.
alsoWhy: Over many years, more than 1,500 µg a day may weaken bones. Keep preformed vitamin A below this.

flags.label: magnesium
flags.why: Magnesium supplements or antacids can stop bone tablets such as alendronate being absorbed. Take them at least 2 hours apart.
alsoWhy: If you take a bone medicine, keep magnesium at least 2 hours away from it.

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: Consider 10 mcg (400 IU) a day. Your doctor may advise more if you are low.

habits.title: Do weight-bearing and strength exercise
habits.why: These help bone strength. Check with your doctor first if you have osteoporosis.

habits.title: Do strength and balance exercises to prevent falls
habits.why: US experts recommend exercise to prevent falls in adults 65 and over at higher risk.

conditions.name: Vegan or vegetarian diet
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you follow a vegan or vegetarian diet, or eat little or no meat, fish, eggs or dairy?

flags.label: collagen
flags.why: Collagen and gelatin come from animals such as fish, cows, pigs or chickens.

flags.label: protein
flags.why: Mix different plant protein foods through the day to cover all essential amino acids.

flags.label: iron
flags.why: People on vegetarian diets need about 1.8 times more iron.
alsoWhy: Plant iron is absorbed less well, so needs are 1.8 times higher; check your level before taking pills.

flags.label: vitamin_b12
flags.why: B12 comes naturally only from animal foods. Vegans need fortified foods or a supplement.
alsoWhy: B12 is only found naturally in animal foods. Vegans need fortified foods or a supplement.

flags.label: iodine
flags.why: Vegans may not get enough iodine. Use fortified foods or a supplement, but avoid kelp and seaweed products.
alsoWhy: Diets with little dairy, eggs or seafood are often low in iodine.

flags.label: zinc
flags.why: Plant foods contain phytates that reduce zinc absorption.
alsoWhy: Phytates in grains and beans lower zinc absorption.

flags.label: calcium
flags.why: Use calcium-fortified dairy alternatives or other good plant sources.
alsoWhy: People who avoid dairy are more likely to be low; use fortified foods or tofu set with calcium.

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: Consider a daily vitamin D supplement, at least in autumn and winter.

flags.label: selenium
flags.why: Selenium can be harder to get on a vegan diet.

flags.label: vitamin_b2
flags.why: Vegans who consume little milk may be low in riboflavin.
alsoWhy: Milk, eggs and meat are main sources. Vegans and people who eat little dairy can run low.

flags.label: omega_3
flags.why: Eat omega-3 rich nuts and seeds, such as walnuts, every day.
alsoWhy: Plant omega-3 (ALA) turns into EPA and DHA poorly (under 15%). Algal oil gives DHA.

flags.label: creatine
flags.why: Vegetarians have lower muscle creatine stores and may gain more from creatine.

habits.title: Plan meals with fortified dairy alternatives, beans, pulses, nuts and seeds
habits.why: With good planning, a vegan diet can give the nutrients you need.

habits.title: Eat vitamin C foods with plant iron sources
habits.why: Vitamin C helps the body absorb iron from plant foods.

conditions.name: Aged 65 or over
conditions.intakeQuestion: Are you aged 65 or over?

flags.label: potassium salt substitutes
flags.why: Salt substitutes with potassium are not advised for older people.

flags.label: potassium
flags.why: Kidneys clear potassium less well with age; only take potassium pills if a doctor advises.

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: In a large trial, vitamin D did not lower fractures in healthy older adults who were not low.
alsoWhy: Consider 10 mcg (400 IU) a day in autumn and winter, or all year if you are frail, housebound or rarely outdoors.
From age 71 the daily need rises to 20 µg (800 IU). Guidelines suggest a daily supplement from age 75.

flags.label: calcium
flags.why: US experts advise against low-dose calcium with vitamin D to prevent fractures in women after menopause who live at home.
alsoWhy: Needs rise to 1,200 mg for women over 50 and men over 70, and the safe limit drops to 2,000 mg.

flags.label: vitamin_a
flags.why: Over many years, more than 1,500 mcg a day of vitamin A may make bones more likely to break. Check multivitamins and fish liver oils.
alsoWhy: Older adults, especially women, should keep long-term vitamin A below 1,500 µg a day to protect bones.

flags.label: magnesium
flags.why: Older adults are more likely to be low, but the risk of too much magnesium rises if kidneys are weak.
alsoWhy: Older adults often eat less magnesium, absorb less and lose more in urine.

flags.label: vitamin_b3
flags.why: Flushing from niacin can drop blood pressure and cause dizziness or falls.

flags.label: vitamin_b9
flags.why: Low B12 is more common with age, and high folic acid can hide it. Stay under 1,000 µg folic acid.

flags.label: iron
flags.why: Older adults rarely need iron pills; low iron at this age needs a doctor to find the cause.

flags.label: iodine
flags.why: Older adults are more sensitive to too much iodine. Avoid high-dose iodine or kelp products.

flags.label: manganese
flags.why: UK experts suggest older people keep manganese from supplements to 0.5 mg a day.

flags.label: probiotics
flags.why: Studies have not shown a clear benefit for antibiotic diarrhoea in people over 65.

flags.label: vitamin_b12
flags.why: About 8 to 9% of adults aged 65 and over have a stomach condition that lowers B12 absorption. Ask about a B12 test, especially if you take metformin or stomach acid tablets.
alsoWhy: The body absorbs less B12 from food with age, so fortified foods or a supplement help.

flags.label: protein
flags.why: Older adults need more protein than younger adults, about 1.0 to 1.2 g per kg of body weight a day, unless they have severe kidney disease.
alsoWhy: Older adults are advised at least 1.0–1.2 g per kg a day to keep muscle, more if active or unwell.

flags.label: vitamin_b1
flags.why: Up to 2 or 3 in 10 older adults show signs of low B1.

habits.title: Do strength, balance and flexibility exercises at least 2 days a week
habits.why: US experts recommend exercise to prevent falls in adults 65 and over at higher risk of falling.

habits.title: Aim for 150 minutes of moderate activity a week and be active every day
habits.why: This is the national advice for adults aged 65 and over.

habits.title: Eat enough protein and stay active together
habits.why: Experts advise both to help older people keep muscle and function.

doctorQuestions: Should my B12, vitamin D or kidney function be checked?
Are all my medicines and supplements still needed and safe together?

conditions.name: Smoking
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you smoke or use tobacco?

flags.label: beta-carotene supplements
flags.why: In two large trials, beta-carotene supplements increased lung cancer risk in smokers.

flags.label: vitamin_a
flags.why: Supplements with beta-carotene raised lung cancer risk in smokers and former smokers. Avoid them.

flags.label: vitamin_e
flags.why: In a trial of male smokers, vitamin E was linked to more bleeding strokes.
alsoWhy: In a trial of smokers, 50 mg a day was linked to more bleeding strokes. Keep to the daily need.

flags.label: vitamin_b6
flags.why: One large study linked more than 20 mg of B6 a day for years to more lung cancer in men, especially smokers.

flags.label: vitamin_b12
flags.why: One large study linked more than 55 µg of B12 a day for years to more lung cancer in men, especially smokers.

flags.label: vitamin_a
flags.why: If this vitamin A is beta-carotene, avoid it: beta-carotene supplements raised lung cancer risk in smokers.

flags.label: vitamin_c
flags.why: Smokers need 35 mg more vitamin C a day. Food is the best source.
alsoWhy: Smokers need 35 mg more vitamin C each day.

habits.title: Get support to stop smoking
habits.why: Free stop smoking services and tools can help you quit.

doctorQuestions: What stop-smoking support or medicine could help me?

conditions.name: Gout
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you had gout, or been told your uric acid is high?

flags.label: vitamin_b3
flags.why: Doctors stop high-dose niacin if acute gout develops.
alsoWhy: Doctors check uric acid on high-dose niacin and stop it if gout flares. Keep to normal amounts.

flags.label: diets or supplements sold for gout
flags.why: UK guidance says there is not enough evidence that any specific diet prevents gout flares or lowers uric acid.

flags.label: molybdenum
flags.why: Very high molybdenum intakes have been linked to gout-like joint pain and high uric acid.

habits.title: Keep to a healthy weight and avoid heavy drinking
habits.why: Excess weight and alcohol may make gout flares worse.

habits.title: Drink enough fluids
habits.why: Being dehydrated can trigger a gout attack.

conditions.name: Inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis)
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis?

flags.label: probiotics
flags.why: Probiotics can rarely cause serious infections in people with weak immune systems, for example on strong immune-suppressing medicines.
alsoWhy: Guidelines advise probiotics for Crohn's or colitis only within research studies.

flags.label: iron
flags.why: Bowel disease can cause low iron, but iron pills can upset the gut; your doctor should choose the type and dose.

flags.label: vitamin_b12
flags.why: Some bowel operations, such as removing the end of the small bowel, are a common risk factor for low B12.
alsoWhy: Bowel disease or bowel surgery can affect B12 absorption.

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis can reduce vitamin D absorption.
alsoWhy: Crohn's disease and colitis can reduce vitamin D absorption. Ask about a blood test.

flags.label: iron
flags.why: Conditions such as ulcerative colitis can reduce iron absorption.

flags.label: zinc
flags.why: 15 to 40% of people with inflammatory bowel disease have low zinc.
alsoWhy: Bowel disease can lower zinc; ask your doctor to check before taking more than the RDA.

flags.label: magnesium
flags.why: Crohn's disease and bowel surgery can lower magnesium.
alsoWhy: Long-term diarrhoea and poor absorption can lower magnesium over time.

flags.label: vitamin_a
flags.why: Crohn's disease and colitis can cause low vitamin A. Ask your doctor about a check.

flags.label: vitamin_e
flags.why: Crohn's disease can reduce fat absorption, which can lead to low vitamin E.

flags.label: vitamin_k
flags.why: Crohn's disease and colitis can lower vitamin K absorption.

flags.label: potassium
flags.why: Bowel disease can cause potassium loss; ask your doctor to check rather than self-treating.

flags.label: vitamin_b3
flags.why: Bowel disease can lead to low niacin.

flags.label: vitamin_b6
flags.why: Crohn's disease and colitis often lower B6 levels.

flags.label: vitamin_b9
flags.why: Many people with bowel disease are low in folate, and some bowel medicines block it.

habits.title: Ask for diet and nutrition advice
habits.why: UK guidance says people with Crohn's disease should be given information on diet and nutrition.

doctorQuestions: Should my iron, B12, vitamin D and zinc be checked?
Are supplements safe with my immune-suppressing medicines?

conditions.name: Coeliac disease
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have coeliac disease?

flags.label: iron
flags.why: Coeliac disease can cause low iron. A GP or dietitian may advise supplements if needed.
alsoWhy: Coeliac disease can stop iron being absorbed; ask your doctor to check your level.

flags.label: vitamin_b12
flags.why: Coeliac disease is a common risk factor for low B12.
alsoWhy: Coeliac disease raises the risk of low B12.

flags.label: vitamin_b9
flags.why: Coeliac disease can cause low folate.
alsoWhy: Coeliac disease can reduce folate absorption.

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: Coeliac disease can reduce vitamin D absorption.
alsoWhy: Coeliac disease can reduce vitamin D absorption. Ask about a blood test.

flags.label: calcium
flags.why: Coeliac disease can be linked to weak bones; your doctor may check whether you need a bone scan.

flags.label: copper
flags.why: In one study, 15% of people with coeliac disease had low copper.
alsoWhy: Poor absorption can lead to low copper. In one study about 1 in 7 people with coeliac disease were low.

flags.label: vitamin_a
flags.why: Newly diagnosed coeliac disease can cause low vitamin A. Ask your doctor about a check.

flags.label: vitamin_k
flags.why: Coeliac disease can lower vitamin K absorption.

flags.label: zinc
flags.why: Coeliac disease can lower zinc absorption; ask your doctor to check.

flags.label: vitamin_b6
flags.why: Coeliac disease can lower B6 absorption.

flags.label: magnesium
flags.why: Poor absorption in coeliac disease can lower magnesium over time.

habits.title: Follow a strict gluten-free diet, with help from a dietitian
habits.why: This is the main treatment. Symptoms usually improve within weeks.

conditions.name: Weight-loss surgery
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you had weight-loss surgery, such as a gastric bypass or sleeve gastrectomy?

flags.label: vitamin_b9
flags.why: If you are planning a pregnancy, ask your surgery team for advice on folic acid and other nutrients.

flags.label: vitamin_b12
flags.why: Many weight-loss operations reduce B12 absorption.
alsoWhy: Weight-loss surgery cuts B12 absorption. You may need high doses or injections, so follow your team's plan.

flags.label: vitamin_b1
flags.why: Severe thiamin deficiency can happen after weight-loss surgery and can damage the brain and nerves.
alsoWhy: Weight-loss surgery can cause serious B1 shortage. Follow your surgical team's vitamin plan.

flags.label: vitamin_d
flags.why: Gastric bypass reduces vitamin D absorption.
alsoWhy: Gastric bypass can lead to low vitamin D. Ask about regular blood tests.

flags.label: iron
flags.why: After weight-loss surgery, nutrition needs special attention from your care team.
alsoWhy: Stomach surgery can reduce iron absorption; your care team should check your level.

flags.label: zinc
flags.why: Zinc can be poorly absorbed, or lost in urine, after weight-loss surgery.
alsoWhy: Weight-loss surgery can lower zinc; your care team should check your level.

flags.label: vitamin_k
flags.why: Weight-loss surgery can lower vitamin K absorption.

flags.label: copper
flags.why: Copper levels can drop after weight-loss surgery. Ask your care team to test.

habits.title: Take the supplements your surgery team prescribes, and keep up follow-up checks
habits.why: Guidelines stress special attention to nutrition after weight-loss surgery.

conditions.name: Having cancer treatment
conditions.intakeQuestion: Are you having treatment for cancer now, such as chemotherapy, radiotherapy, hormone therapy or targeted drugs?

flags.label: St John's wort
flags.why: It can weaken some cancer medicines.

flags.label: vitamin_c
flags.why: Ask your cancer team before taking vitamin C or other antioxidants, especially in high doses, during chemotherapy or radiotherapy.
alsoWhy: High-dose antioxidants might affect chemotherapy or radiotherapy. Ask your cancer team first.

flags.label: vitamin_e
flags.why: Cancer doctors often advise against antioxidant supplements during chemotherapy or radiotherapy, because they might make treatment work less well.
alsoWhy: Antioxidants like vitamin E might make chemotherapy or radiotherapy work less well. Ask your cancer team first.

flags.label: turmeric
flags.why: Talk to your cancer team first. Curcumin may interact with some chemotherapy medicines.

flags.label: vitamin_b9
flags.why: If you take methotrexate for cancer, ask your cancer doctor before taking folic acid, as it could interfere with treatment.
alsoWhy: Folate can weaken some cancer drugs, such as methotrexate. Ask your cancer team first.

flags.label: coq10
flags.why: CoQ10 may not be compatible with some types of cancer treatment.
alsoWhy: CoQ10 may not mix well with some cancer treatments.

flags.label: probiotics
flags.why: In people with weak immune systems, probiotics have rarely caused serious blood infections.
alsoWhy: If treatment has weakened your immune system, probiotics carry a higher infection risk.

flags.label: vitamin_b1
flags.why: Some chemotherapy can cause B1 shortage. Ask your cancer team before taking supplements.

flags.label: iron
flags.why: Cancer can cause low iron, but your treatment team should decide on any iron.

flags.label: selenium
flags.why: Some chemotherapy lowers selenium, and selenium does not prevent cancer. Ask your cancer team first.
alsoWhy: Cisplatin, a chemotherapy medicine, can lower selenium, but it is not clear whether this matters or whether supplements help.

flags.label: boron
flags.why: Small studies show boron can change estrogen and testosterone levels, so check with your cancer team first.

flags.label: protein
flags.why: Protein needs often change during treatment; follow your care team's advice.

flags.label: ashwagandha
flags.why: It may raise testosterone, which may be unsafe in hormone-sensitive prostate cancer.

flags.label: nmn
flags.why: Trials mainly involved generally healthy adults; check with your care team.

habits.title: Show your cancer team every supplement before you start it
habits.why: Some supplements, especially antioxidants, may change how cancer treatments work.
